static_review: HMAC pad init 0x36 and key xor is equivalent for empty, short and hashed long keys; repeated 0x6a u64 xor has no endianness dependency.
zero_tail checks each complete 8-byte word and all remainder bytes without aligned reads or out-of-bounds loads.
new, decode and update preserve canonical zero tail; sum consumes its context, so full tail copies preserve state semantics.

Pinned generic-array representation has valid byte-only repr(C)/repr(transparent) layout; size/alignment assertions, complete input block bounds and scoped immutable borrows justify bulk compress casts.
write_state writes all bytes in disjoint ranges: 0..32,32..64,64..72,72..136 for SHA256 and 0..64,64..128,128..144,144..272 for SHA512.
Raw write_unaligned(value.to_be()) is equivalent to to_be_bytes copies; no references to uninitialized output are made; temporary count bytes live through copy calls.
Compiler output allocation remains fresh and managed; public HMAC module and compiler implementations unchanged.
